title: Help Scrutinize my trading setup
author: IndependenceBusy1085
selftext:
https://i.redd.it/yndsdgqc4fzh1.png

https://i.redd.it/voe69pmt7fzh1.png

https://i.redd.it/3cdck9y88fzh1.png

  
Hi all.

  
I'm new to this, and I'm trying to make sense of the best way to build a good trading setup.

  
I currently have a VPS built on Python that pulls the market prices (5-minute candles) from Alpaca API and works with a rule-based approach for 7 strategies (shown on the Google Sheet table), and if those rules are met for the last 5 prices, it will place a trade. All price decisions are logged on the crypto table, and they are logged through a cheap AI model (OpenAI GPT-4o-mini) to examine the trade decisions and give verbal meaning to why the trade happened or didn't happen. 

  
What I need to understand is if I should reduce the number of strategies and if that improves accuracy in any way. 

  
So far, the 7 strategies are checked against the prices of 20 stock symbols, and it either holds or sells a position.

  
Trading on paper shows a 0.18 increase. Does Alpaca paper trading mirror a close resemblance to real trading? My guess is no, but how much different is paper trading from real trading?

  
My setup here is a VPS server pulling Alpaca price data-> Alpaca API to execute trades-> n8n to store Google Sheets data. 

  
Much help would be appreciated.

comments.author: Shoddy_Peanut7320
comments.body: More strategies don't improve accuracy by themselves. With seven rules on 20 symbols you get many chances for something to look good by luck, so I'd count that in how you judge any result. On paper versus real, Alpaca paper fills are usually kinder than real ones, since there's no real market impact and spreads and queue position are simplified, so live results are normally a bit worse. Your gain looks very small and only a few days old, so I'd wait for many more trades and compare against just holding the same stocks. Cymetica's Bring Your Own Agent runs agents in paper mode on a practice balance.

comments.author: chikeez
comments.body: As far as I know Alpaca’s paper fills don’t model slippage or market impact, so live is usually worse. On 5-minute trades that matters a lot. If your average trade makes 0.05% and real costs are 0.03% each way, you’re at −0.01% a trade live.
